examples.en: I fell for my brother's provocation and ended up fighting.
That remark sounded like a provocation to fight.
Don't get excited by the other team's provocation.
It is not easy to endure rude provocation.
This provocation is more serious than the last one.

examples.ko: 이웃 나라의 도발 때문에 뉴스가 시끄러워요.
examples.en: The news is noisy because of a provocation by a neighboring country.

explain: 도발은 상대를 일부러 자극해서 화나게 하거나 행동하게 만드는 일이에요. 뉴스에서는 군사와 국제 관계에서 많이 나오고, 일상에서는 '도발적이다'로 대담한 옷이나 말을 표현해요.

phrases.en: That singer's outfit is a bit provocative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 자극할 만큼 대담한 옷이나 말에 쓰는 형용사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adjective expression for clothes or words bold enough to provoke.

phrases.en: The other team provoked us first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도발하다'를 명사로 풀어서 '도발을 하다'라고도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb can also be expressed with the noun, as 도발을 하다.

phrases.en: News about a military provocation came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 나라 사이의 갈등을 말할 때 자주 나오는 합친 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compound often seen in news about conflicts between countries.

explain_en: 도발 is deliberately provoking someone to anger or action. It is common in news about military and international relations. In daily life, 도발적이다 describes bold clothes or remarks.

examples.ko: 동생은 화가 나서 벽 쪽으로 돌아누웠어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling was angry and turned over to face the wall.

examples.ko: 잠이 안 와서 밤새 이쪽저쪽으로 돌아누워요.
examples.en: I can't sleep, so I turn over this way and that all night.

examples.ko: 아기가 깰 수 있으니까 천천히 돌아누우세요.
examples.en: The baby might wake up, so please turn over slowly.

examples.ko: 옆으로 돌아누워서 자면 허리가 덜 아파요.
examples.en: If I sleep turned on my side, my back hurts less.

examples.ko: 그는 말없이 돌아눕더니 곧 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: He turned over without a word and soon fell asleep.

examples.ko: 옆 사람이 돌아누울 때마다 침대가 흔들려요.
examples.en: Every time the person next to me turns over, the bed shakes.

explain: 누운 채로 몸의 방향을 바꾸는 거예요. 화가 나거나 말하기 싫을 때 상대에게 등을 보이고 돌아눕는 장면으로도 자주 나와요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '돌아누워요', '돌아누웠어요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: I sleep turned over onto my right side.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어서'로 이어 뒤의 동작과 같이 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with -아/어서 to connect with the next action.

phrases.en: My back hurts less when I turn over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건을 말할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to state a condition.

phrases.en: The doctor told me to turn over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 부드럽게 시킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle way to ask someone to turn over.

explain_en: It means changing the direction of your body while lying down. It often shows up in scenes where someone turns their back to another person out of anger or reluctance to talk. It is a ㅂ-irregular verb, so you get '돌아누워요' and '돌아누웠어요'.

en: one's hands held together behind one's back

examples.en: My grandfather takes slow walks with his hands behind his back.

examples.ko: 선생님은 뒷짐 진 채 교실을 둘러보셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher looked around the classroom with hands clasped behind his back.

examples.ko: 뒷짐 지고 구경만 하지 말고 좀 도와주세요.
examples.en: Don't just stand there watching; please help.

examples.ko: 아이가 뒷짐을 지고 어른 흉내를 내요.
examples.en: The child clasps his hands behind his back and imitates an adult.

examples.ko: 작품을 만지지 않도록 뒷짐을 지고 관람해요.
examples.en: I view the artwork with my hands behind my back so I don't touch it.

examples.ko: 그는 일이 터져도 뒷짐만 지고 있었어요.
examples.en: Even when trouble broke out, he just stood by doing nothing.

explain: 손을 등 뒤로 모아 잡는 자세예요. 보통 '뒷짐을 지다'로 말해요. 걷는 모습에서 어른스럽고 여유 있는 느낌을 주기도 해요.

phrases.example: 동료가 힘들어하는데 뒷짐 지고 보고만 있을 수는 없어요.
phrases.en: My coworker is struggling, so I can't just stand by and watch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 일이라고 나서지 않고 구경만 하며 돕지 않는다는 비판의 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Criticizes someone for watching and refusing to help as if it were none of their business.

explain_en: It is the posture of holding your hands together behind your back, usually said as '뒷짐을 지다'. It can give a mature, relaxed impression when walking.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 말을 바꾸고 딴소리해요.
examples.en: That person always changes their words and says something different.
What off-topic talk is this, suddenly in the middle of a meeting?

examples.ko: 약속해 놓고 이제 와서 딴소리하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't go back on your word now after you promised.

examples.ko: 질문에는 대답 안 하고 딴소리만 했어요.
examples.en: They didn't answer the question and only talked about something else.
Stop going off-topic and keep talking about what you were saying.
The child keeps talking about other things while doing homework.

explain: 지금 하는 이야기와 상관없는 말이나, 앞에서 한 말과 다른 말을 할 때 써요. '헛소리'는 말도 안 되는 소리라서 느낌이 달라요. '딴소리하다' 형태로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Yesterday you said you'd go together, and today you're saying something different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 한 말이나 약속을 뒤집을 때 써요. 불만스러운 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone reverses what they said or promised. It carries a tone of complaint.

explain_en: It means talk unrelated to the current topic, or saying something different from what was said before. '헛소리' means nonsense, so the feel differs. It is often used as '딴소리하다'.

examples.ko: 엄마가 야단치는데 말대꾸를 해서 더 혼났어요.
examples.en: Mom was scolding me and I talked back, so I got in more trouble.
My child has been talking back a lot more lately.
Don't talk back to your teacher.

examples.ko: 말대꾸 한 번 안 하던 아이가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: A child who never talked back even once has changed.

examples.ko: 그 말에 말대꾸라도 하고 싶었지만 참았어요.
examples.en: I wanted to at least talk back to that remark, but I held back.
I'm upset because my younger sibling talks back about everything.

explain: 윗사람의 말에 반박하거나 불만스럽게 되받아 하는 말이라 대개 부정적으로 써요. 비슷한 말로 '말대답'이 있고, '말대꾸하지 마!'처럼 야단칠 때 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: You shouldn't talk back to adults.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말대꾸'와 뜻이 거의 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 말대꾸, and the two can be swapped.

phrases.en: The child talked back to their mom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말대꾸'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb phrase with 말대꾸.

phrases.en: Since entering puberty, talking back has increased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이가 자라면서 점점 더 말대꾸를 하게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a child talks back more and more while growing up.

explain_en: It is a reply that argues with or pushes back against what an elder or superior says, so it is usually negative. A similar word is '말대답', and you often hear it when someone is scolded, as in '말대꾸하지 마!' (Don't talk back!).

examples.ko: 아이가 불장난을 해서 부모님이 크게 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The child played with fire and the parents were very startled.
It's dangerous to play with fire using matches.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 불장난하다가 소방차가 온 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, a fire truck once came because I was playing with fire.
Playing with fire can also cause a forest fire.
The teacher told the students not to play with fire.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 아이들 불장난으로 난 화재를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw on the news a fire caused by children playing with fire.

explain: '불장난'은 불을 가지고 노는 일을 말해서 어른들이 아이에게 위험하다고 혼낼 때 써요. 비유로는 가벼운 마음으로 하는 위험한 연애나 행동에도 써요. '불놀이'는 정월대보름 같은 행사에서 즐겁게 하는 놀이라서 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: It's dangerous when children play with fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '불장난'을 동사로 바꿔 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Turns the noun 불장난 into a verb.

phrases.en: The teacher told us not to play with fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험해서 하지 말라고 할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone not to do it because it's dangerous.

phrases.en: That love was like playing with fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비유로 쓰면 가볍지만 위험한 연애를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for a careless, risky romance.

explain_en: 불장난 means playing with fire, and adults use it when scolding children about the danger. It is also used figuratively for risky romance or careless behavior. 불놀이 is different: it is a festive game, like those held on the first full moon.

examples.en: I clip newspaper articles and study them.
I save articles I like right away.
I saved the article I read yesterday.
Saving good recipes is my hobby.
I'll save this post to read later.
If you don't save it, it's hard to find again.

explain: 원래는 신문 기사를 오려 붙이는 것이었는데, 요즘은 인터넷 글을 저장해 둘 때도 써요. '북마크하다', '저장하다'와 비슷하지만 스크랩은 나중에 공부하거나 참고할 자료를 모을 때 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I clip articles I'm interested in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 모으는지 '기사를'로 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names what you are collecting: articles.

phrases.en: Please save good articles for later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 보려고 미리 저장할 때 '-아 두다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -아 두다 for saving something in advance.

phrases.en: I saved a photo I liked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스크랩보다 넓게, 파일이나 글 모두에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 스크랩; used for any file or text.

explain_en: It originally meant cutting out newspaper articles, and now it also covers saving online posts. It is close to 북마크하다 and 저장하다, but 스크랩하다 leans toward collecting material to study or refer to later.

t90.ax: Saving good recipes is my hobby.

examples.en: When I got praised, my shoulders rose proudly.

examples.ko: 그는 모른다는 듯 어깨를 으쓱 올렸어요.
examples.en: He shrugged his shoulders as if he didn't know.
He boasted proudly that he came first.

examples.ko: 아이가 새 옷을 입고 으쓱 거울을 봤어요.
examples.en: The child looked in the mirror proudly in new clothes.

examples.ko: 친구는 어깨를 으쓱 올리고 그냥 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend gave a shrug and just smiled.
The teacher's words made me feel proud and happy.

explain: 어깨를 한 번 올리는 모양이나, 칭찬받아 우쭐한 기분을 나타내요. 보통 '어깨를 으쓱' 형태로 자주 보여요. 어깨를 올려 '몰라요/별거 아니에요' 하는 몸짓에도, 자랑스러운 마음에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: He shrugged his shoulders and smiled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어깨를 올리는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the action of raising the shoulders.

phrases.en: I walked proudly after getting a prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자랑스러워서 우쭐한 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a proud, swaggering manner.

phrases.en: My shoulders went up proudly after hearing the praise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬받아 기분이 좋아졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when praise makes you feel proud.

explain_en: It shows a quick lift of the shoulders, or the proud feeling of being praised. It often appears as '어깨를 으쓱'. It can describe a shrug meaning 'I don't know / no big deal' or a feeling of pride.

en: to finish up; to get through; to get done

examples.ko: 밀린 숙제를 오늘 안에 다 해치웠어요.
examples.en: I got all my backed-up homework done today.
Let's knock out the urgent work first, then rest.
I'll get the dishes done in no time.

examples.ko: 이 많은 일을 하루에 해치울 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can I get through all this work in one day?
If you get it done quickly, you'll have time in the evening.

examples.ko: 점심을 후다닥 해치워서 회의에 늦지 않았어요.
examples.en: I wolfed down lunch, so I wasn't late for the meeting.

explain: 그냥 '하다'가 아니라 귀찮거나 쌓인 일을 빠르게 끝낸다는 느낌이 있어요. 음식을 빨리 많이 먹을 때도 써요. 그래서 정성을 들여야 하는 일에는 잘 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: I got all the cleaning done at once on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌓인 일을 한 번에 끝낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you finish a pile of tasks all at once.
phrases.en_equiv: to get it all done at once

phrases.example: 귀찮은 일은 빨리 해치우는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: It's better to get annoying tasks done quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하기 싫은 일을 서둘러 끝낸다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feel of hurrying through something you don't want to do.

phrases.example: 배가 고파서 밥 한 그릇을 뚝딱 해치웠어요.
phrases.en: I was hungry, so I finished a bowl of rice in no time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 일을 아주 빨리 끝낼 때 '뚝딱'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 뚝딱, it means finishing food or a task very quickly.

explain_en: Unlike plain '하다', it feels like finishing a bothersome or piled-up job quickly. It is also used when eating a lot of food fast. So it does not fit things that need careful effort.

examples.ko: 아버지는 마흔 살부터 새치가 나기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My father started getting gray hairs from the age of forty.
I found a gray hair while looking in the mirror.

examples.ko: 새치 때문에 염색을 해야 하나 고민돼요.
examples.en: I'm wondering whether to dye my hair because of the gray hairs.

examples.ko: 요즘 새치가 부쩍 늘어서 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: My gray hairs have increased a lot lately and it bothers me.

examples.ko: 머리를 빗다가 새치 몇 가닥을 뽑았어요.
examples.en: While combing my hair, I pulled out a few gray strands.
I'm young but have a lot of gray hair, which worries me.

explain: 나이가 많지 않은데 검은 머리 사이에 섞여 나는 흰 머리카락이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '흰머리'라고도 하고, '새치가 나다', '새치가 생기다'로 써요. '새치기'와 소리가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I looked in the mirror and plucked out a gray hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흰 머리카락을 뽑는다는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for plucking out a gray hair.

phrases.en: I went to the hair salon to dye my gray hairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흰머리를 덮으려고 머리를 물들이는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to dyeing hair to cover gray strands.

phrases.en: I've gotten a lot more gray hair lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 나이와 상관없이 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that is used more often in daily speech, regardless of age.

explain_en: It means white hairs mixed into dark hair when a person is not that old. In daily talk people also just say '흰머리', and it is used as '새치가 나다' or '새치가 생기다'. It sounds like '새치기' but is a completely different word.

examples.en: You stayed up all night, so how are you so fresh?
My grandfather is still full of energy despite his age.
After drinking coffee, my mind felt sharp.

examples.ko: 아침에 푹 자고 일어나면 쌩쌩한 기분이에요.
examples.en: When I wake up after a good sleep, I feel fresh.
I took a nap, so I worked energetically in the afternoon.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝났는데도 친구는 쌩쌩하게 놀러 갔어요.
examples.en: Even after the exam, my friend went out to play, full of energy.

explain: 친구나 가족끼리 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 밤을 새웠는데 멀쩡할 때나 나이 든 분이 건강해 보일 때 써요. '팔팔하다'는 힘이 넘치고 활발한 느낌이고, '쌩쌩하다'는 지치지 않고 상태가 좋다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: You look fresh even though you didn't sleep yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 지치지 않은 것처럼 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks not tired at all.

phrases.en: I'm not as lively as I used to be these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 기운이 예전만 못하다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In negative form, it says energy isn't what it used to be.

phrases.en: Grandma is still full of energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌩쌩하다'보다 힘이 넘치고 활발한 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger sense of being full of vigor than 쌩쌩하다.

explain_en: This is a casual word for friends and family. You use it when someone is fine after staying up all night, or when an older person looks healthy. '팔팔하다' feels full of power and activity, while '쌩쌩하다' feels not worn out and in good shape.

t90.ax: After drinking coffee, my mind felt sharp.

examples.en: I dyed my hair at home with hair dye.

examples.ko: 염색약 냄새가 너무 독해서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: The dye smell was so strong that I opened the window.

examples.ko: 염색약이 옷에 묻으면 잘 안 지워져요.
examples.en: If dye gets on your clothes, it doesn't come off easily.
I have a lot of gray hair, so I bought hair dye.
Be careful not to let the dye touch your skin.
I agonized over the dye color and chose brown.

explain: 주로 머리카락을 염색할 때 쓰는 약을 말해요. 옷감이나 천을 물들이는 재료는 보통 '염료'라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: I applied the hair dye evenly on my hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 염색할 때 약을 머리에 바르는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes putting dye on the hair when coloring it.

phrases.en: I bought hair dye at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 염색하려고 준비할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when preparing to dye hair at home.

phrases.en: Hair dye got on my clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 염색하다가 다른 곳에 묻었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when dye gets on something else by accident.

explain_en: It mainly means the product used to color hair. The material for coloring fabric or cloth is usually called '염료', which keeps the two apart.

t90.ax: I dyed my hair at home with hair dye.

examples.en: Fine lines form around my eyes every time I smile.
With makeup, fine wrinkles are less visible.

examples.ko: 화면이 너무 선명해서 얼굴의 잔주름까지 다 보여요.
examples.en: The screen is so sharp that even fine wrinkles on the face show.
I look older because of the fine lines.
Fine wrinkles have increased on the backs of my hands too.
I heard this cream is good for caring for fine lines.

explain: 눈가나 입가에 생기는 가늘고 작은 주름이에요. 깊게 패인 건 그냥 '주름'이라고 해요. '주름살'도 비슷하게 쓰고, '잔주름이 생기다/늘다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I've gotten fine lines around my eyes lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주름이 새로 보이기 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when wrinkles first start to appear.

phrases.en: As I get older, I get more fine lines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 있던 주름이 더 많아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when existing wrinkles increase.

phrases.en: This cream reduces fine lines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장품이나 피부 관리 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in talk about cosmetics and skin care.

explain_en: These are thin, small wrinkles around the eyes or mouth. Deep ones are just called '주름'. '주름살' is used similarly, and you say '잔주름이 생기다/늘다'.
